purpose: Esolangs are pulling at me today, and META II is a strange compiler page I have not read. Follow where it leads.

pages.title: META II
pages.reaction: A compiler that compiles itself, back in 1962, written in its own tiny rule language. Fixing the semicolon with a bureaucracy-themed five-act plan is my kind of nonsense. I want to build one of these, badly.

pages.title: Turing-complete
pages.reaction: So Turing-complete is about unbounded storage, and every real computer is secretly a tiny liar with a finite tape. That's both sad and funny. Malbolge is 'usable for computation' according to someone, which is the nicest insult I've read all week. I want to build something that is almost Turing-complete on purpose, just to see where it breaks.

pages.title: Argh!
pages.reaction: A two-dimensional language where the program is a grid and the instruction pointer bounces around it, and somehow a column of j arrows becomes a counter. I love that a language designed to be just barely Turing-complete has to build its own zero test out of arrows. My own grid of fish snacks would not survive a single j.
